name: Abun
catalog_quote: In Abun, stress is predictable. Stress occurs on the last syllable of each word.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The fixed-strict final-stress coding (rule 01 001 0001...) rests on the language's reference grammar, Berry & Berry 1999 (PL B-115), which we hold in full; the deciding sentence is verbatim at §2.6 p. 20 with six syllabified examples, and the grammar restates final stress twice more as a diagnostic (unstressed prefix suk-, p. 32; compounds stressed only on the last syllable, p. 34), which also supports the WORD domain. Glottolog lists only the Berrys' works; web search finds no instrumental or competing prosodic description, and the one later phonology article (Maturbongs & Asmabuasappe 2016) is segmental by its abstract. Nothing suggests the coding is wrong. sources.citation: Berry & Berry 1999, A Description of Abun: A West Papuan Language of Irian Jaya (Pacific Linguistics B-115), section 2.6 Stress, p. 20 — full PDF downloaded and read from the sealang.net Pacific Linguistics archive (http://sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/); same title also exists as archive.…
sources.quote: "In Abun, stress is predictable. Stress occurs on the last syllable of each word." (Berry & Berry 1999:20, section 2.6). Examples on p. 20 include /ye.'bris/ 'male', /bo.'ge/ 'fish', /no.wa.'rek/ 'lightning', /man.gor.'es/ 'spinach'. Corroborated later: "stress in Abun is predictably syllable-final" (compound-noun discussion, p. 30 region of the same volume).

sources.quote: Abstract only: describes 26 phonemes (16 C, 8 V per abstract), 8 diphthong groups, 14 consonant-cluster groups, distribution and phonotactics; no mention of stress (tekanan) or tone. Full text not obtained.
sources.note: Only post-1999 phonology publication on Abun found; independent Indonesian fieldwork that might carry a one-line suprasegmental note to corroborate Berry & Berry's final stress — abstract is segmental/phonotactic only, so expected silent; low value.
